sketch: Each Yeet lane would emit a canonical, DSSE-style envelope keyed to the exact PR head and base SHA, containing the lane-definition digest, a Merkle root of its declared input closure, command and toolchain/container identities, result, and output-log digest. A hardware-backed workstation key registered to the repository would sign that envelope, and `yeet publish` would upload the bundle to immutable storage indexed by the head SHA rather than commit it into the tree it describes. Hosted CI would verify the signature and policy, recompute the lane definition and input root from the checkout, and reject any seal whose base, inputs, toolchain policy, or signer authorization no longer matches. It would then derive an unpredictable audit sample from server-side entropy revealed only after upload, rerun those lanes plus every invalidated or unsealed lane, and compare rerun results with their attestations. Initially the mechanism should run in shadow mode beside the full battery, measuring false reuse and cross-environment disagreement before any required job is skipped. Because squash merges and operator-controlled merge order continually change the base SHA, attestations should be reusable across a rebase only when the recomputed dependency closure is identical; otherwise Yeet must reseal the affected lanes.
risk: The load-bearing risk is an unsound input-closure model: one undeclared file, environment dependency, generated artifact, or cross-lane side effect can make a valid signature certify a result that is no longer valid, while random spot checks may miss it.
first_step: Add a versioned Effect Schema for a lane attestation and instrument one deterministic lane, such as typecheck, to emit unsigned canonical envelopes in CI shadow mode; compare its declared input root against full reruns before introducing signing or skip decisions.

children.text: Use audit failures as an automatic trust ratchet: quarantine that lane or signer and temporarily restore 100% hosted execution until a clean streak rebuilds confidence.
Make sampling risk-weighted rather than uniform, increasing audit probability for flaky lanes, broad dependency closures, new toolchains, first-time contributors, and security-sensitive packages.
Chain lane attestations into a PR-level provenance graph so downstream lanes can cite exact upstream artifacts and hosted CI can rerun only the invalidated subgraph.
Reuse unchanged attestations across stacked PRs or operator-reordered merges by proving identical input closures, turning merge-order churn into selective resealing rather than a full proof restart.
Publish aggregate verification statistics and mismatch causes, creating an evidence-based path to tune lane boundaries, hermeticity, and the minimum hosted audit rate.
